words.gloss: apāṅga (outer corner of the eye); kanīna (inner corner or pupil of the eye, probable)

hindi: और दो, अपांग यानी आँख के बाहरी कोने और कनीन यानी सम्भवतः आँख के भीतरी कोने में।
english: And two, at the apāṅga (outer corner of the eye) and the kanīna (probably the inner corner of the eye).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the preceding unit (86, outside this chunk), which presumably names the thing counted; the noun counted is not stated here and is not supplied. kanīna (cf. kanīnikā) is probably the inner corner or pupil of the eye; the exact sense is not firm. Case of the dual -nayoḥ taken as locative ('at'); genitive is possible.

hindi: इस प्रकार वे छह हैं।
english: Thus these are six.
notes: Copula understood. 'te' points back to the items counted in 86-87 (not named in this unit); GROUPING: appears to complete the count begun in 86-87.

hindi: और छह पटल यानी परतें।
english: And six paṭalas (layers).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. paṭala = layer, coat (here of the eye, from the context of 87-94; the eye is not named in this line).

hindi: दो वर्त्म यानी पलकें।
english: Two vartmas (eyelids).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. vartman = eyelid in the eye-section (standard); it also means 'path'.

hindi: बाहरी और अग्नि तथा जल पर आश्रित; दूसरा मांस, तीसरा मेद यानी चर्बी, चौथा अस्थि यानी हड्डी; उनकी मोटाई दृष्टि के पाँचवें अंश से है।
english: The outer one, and one resting on fire (agni) and water; the second, flesh; the third, fat (medas); the fourth, bone; their thickness is by a fifth part of sight (dṛṣṭi).

text_flags.why: possible: the full stop printed between the words stands for a space or a lost punctuation mark

notes: Elliptical and compressed: the noun (probably paṭala, 'layer', from 89) is not stated and is not supplied; 'their' (teṣām) is taken to refer to those unnamed items. The first part is hard: 'bāhyam ca āśritam agnyambhasī' is read as 'the outer one, and one resting on fire and water' (two descriptions of the first item, or two items); not settled. 'dvitīyam' is read with the series that follows (second: flesh, third: fat, fourth: bone). 'bahulatā' = thickness or abundance; 'dṛṣṭeḥ pañcamāṃśena' ('by a fifth part of sight') is kept literal and not interpreted. Print: 'cāśritamagnyaṃbhasīdvitīyaṃ' = ca āśritam agni-ambhasī dvitīyam (split is probable, not certain).
lines_deva: बाह्यं चाश्रितमग्न्यंभसीद्वितीयं मांसं.तृतीयं मेदश्चतुर्थमस्थि तेषां बहुलता दृष्टेः पंचमांशेन
lines_iast: bāhyaṃ cāśritamagnyaṃbhasīdvitīyaṃ māṃsaṃ.tṛtīyaṃ medaścaturthamasthi teṣāṃ bahulatā dṛṣṭeḥ paṃcamāṃśena

words.gloss: sirā (vein, vessel; standard); kaṇḍarā (large tendon; standard); fat (medas); Kapha; having the nature of

hindi: बन्धन के गुण यानी रज्जु तो चार हैं, जिनका स्वरूप सिरा यानी नस, कण्डरा यानी मोटा स्नायु-रज्जु, मेद और कफ है।
english: The binding strands (bandhana-guṇa), however, are four, having the nature of sirā (vein, vessel), kaṇḍarā (large tendon), fat (medas) and Kapha.
notes: guṇa is read as 'strand, cord' (that which binds); 'quality' is the other possible sense and is not adopted. sirā = vein or vessel (standard); kaṇḍarā = large tendon (standard). Kapha is capitalised as the doṣa. 'ātmaka' = having as its nature, consisting of.

hindi: और वह बिजली की तरह और वड़वामुख यानी समुद्र की भीतरी अग्नि की तरह जल के मध्य में स्थित होकर भी वीर्य यानी शक्ति की प्रबलता से अपने तेजत्व को नहीं छोड़ता।
english: And that (tejas), like lightning and like the vaḍavāmukha (the submarine fire), even when situated in the midst of water, does not abandon its fiery nature (tejastva) because of the excellence of its vīrya (potency).
notes: 'tat' is taken as the tejas of 94. vaḍavāmukha = the fire of the mare's mouth, said to burn under the ocean (standard in Sanskrit literature). Print: 'vīryyotkarṣāt' has doubled y (print habit, normalised once). 'vaidyutavat' = 'like the lightning (fire)'.

hindi: मांस, रक्त और कफ के प्रसाद यानी सार अंश से तो जिह्वा उत्पन्न होती है।
english: From the clear essence (prasāda) of flesh, blood and Kapha, however, the tongue (jihvā) arises.

text_flags.why: near certain: standard spelling is jihvā; hv/vh letter reversal in this print, normalised in `w` (also in unit 104)

notes: prasāda = clear, pure part (the finest part); the word is kept literal. asṛk = blood. The same letter reversal jivhā occurs in unit 104 and is normalised there without a new flag.

words.gloss: flesh; blood; Kapha; fat; clear essence

hindi: मांस, रक्त, कफ और मेद के प्रसाद यानी सार अंश से दो वृषण यानी अण्डकोश के गोलक।
english: From the clear essence (prasāda) of flesh, blood, Kapha and fat, the two testes (vṛṣaṇa).
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'arise' (jāyete) is carried from 96 and is not supplied. The closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement and is not translated.

words.gloss: tongue; binding (the binding of the tongue; sense uncertain)

hindi: प्राण के दस आयतन यानी आश्रय स्थान हैं: मूर्धा यानी सिर, जिह्वाबन्धन यानी जीभ का बन्धन, कण्ठ, हृदय, नाभि, बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय, गूद यानी गुदा, शुक्र यानी वीर्य नामक प्रजनन-द्रव, ओज और रक्त।
english: There are ten seats of life (prāṇāyatana): the head (mūrdhan), the jihvābandhana (tongue-binding), the throat, the heart (hṛdaya), the navel, the bladder (basti), the gūda (anus, rectum), śukra (semen), ojas and blood.
notes: Ten items are named: head, tongue-binding, throat, heart, navel, bladder, gūda, śukra, ojas, blood. 'jihvābandhana' is kept literal ('tongue-binding'); it may mean the root of the tongue or the frenulum, which is not settled. 'kaṇṭha' may mean neck or throat. basti = bladder here (standard); gūda = anus or rectum. Print: 'mūrddhā' has doubled d (normalised to mūrdhā, a print habit). ojas is a doctrinal term and is not forced into a modern equivalent.
lines_deva: दश प्राणायतनानि मूर्द्धा जिह्वाबंधनं कंठो हृदयं नाभिर्बस्तिर्गूदः शुक्रमोजो रक्तं
lines_iast: daśa prāṇāyatanāni mūrddhā jihvābaṃdhanaṃ kaṃṭho hṛdayaṃ nābhirbastirgūdaḥ śukramojo raktaṃ

hindi: सोलह कण्डराएँ हैं; उनमें से हाथों और पैरों में दो-दो, गर्दन और पीठ में चार, अलग-अलग।
english: There are sixteen kaṇḍarās (large tendons); of them, two each in the hands and feet, four, separately, in the neck and the back.
notes: Copula understood. 'dve dve' is distributive ('two each'). Taken together the numbers make sixteen only if 'four' belongs to each of neck and back (8 + 4 + 4); the Sanskrit says only 'four, separately' and no 'each' is added. Counts are translated as printed.
lines_deva: षोडश कंडराः तासां द्वे द्वे करचरणेषु चतस्रः पृथकग्रीवापृष्ठयोः
lines_iast: ṣoḍaśa kaṃḍarāḥ tāsāṃ dve dve karacaraṇeṣu catasraḥ pṛthakagrīvāpṛṣṭhayoḥ

words.gloss: flesh; vessel; snāyu (ligament, sinew); bone; born of

hindi: सोलह जाल हैं; उनमें मांस, सिरा, स्नायु और अस्थि से उत्पन्न, एक-एक स्थान पर चार, गुल्फ यानी टखने और मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई में, परस्पर झरोखेदार स्थित हैं।
english: There are sixteen jālas (nets); of them, those born of flesh, vessel, snāyu (ligament) and bone, four in each single place, at the ankle (gulpha) and the wrist (maṇibandha), are situated mutually latticed.
notes: jāla = net, mesh (a doctrinal structure; no firm modern equivalent). The four kinds (flesh, vessel, snāyu, bone) are read as the four per site; with four sites (two ankles, two wrists) the total is sixteen, but that sum is not stated. 'gavākṣita' = made like a window (gavākṣa, lattice), i.e. interlaced; the sense is kept literal. 'gulpha' = ankle, 'maṇibandha' = wrist (both standard). 'ca' joins the two sites.
lines_deva: षोडश जालानि तेषां मांससिरास्नाय्वस्थिजानि चत्वार्य्येकैकत्र गुल्फे मणिबंधे च परस्परगवाक्षितानि स्थितानि
lines_iast: ṣoḍaśa jālāni teṣāṃ māṃsasirāsnāyvasthijāni catvāryyekaikatra gulphe maṇibaṃdhe ca parasparagavākṣitāni sthitāni

hindi: छह कूर्च हैं: हाथों, पैरों, गर्दन और मेढ्र यानी शिश्न में।
english: Six kūrcas (bundles, sense uncertain): in the hands, feet, neck and penis (meḍhra).

text_flags.why: possible: before h the visarga of kūrcāḥ should remain; the printed -ā looks like a dropped visarga

notes: Elliptical: copula understood and not supplied. kūrca = tuft, bundle (as a body part it is not firmly identified; the same word names a part of the foot in 111). The line does not say how the six are shared among the places. Print: doubled cc in 'kūrccā' is a print habit (normalised).

words.gloss: sīmantas (partings; here probably sutures of bone)

hindi: उसी प्रकार सीमन्त यानी सम्भवतः अस्थियों की सीवन-रेखाएँ; वे तो पाँच सिर में, इस प्रकार अठारह।
english: Likewise the sīmantas (probably sutures of bones); they, however, are five in the head: thus eighteen.
notes: Elliptical: copula understood. 'Likewise' refers to the places listed in 106, and eighteen is probably twelve limb places + trika + five in the head (a reading, not stated). 'sīmanta' = hair-parting; as a bone term, a suture (probable). Printed 'śirasītyaṣṭādaśa' = śirasi iti aṣṭādaśa.

words.gloss: forty; hundred (that is, one hundred and forty)

hindi: और उनमें से एक सौ चालीस शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में, एक सौ बीस अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में, सौ सिर में।
english: And of them, a hundred and forty in the limbs (śākhā), a hundred and twenty in the trunk (antarādhi), a hundred in the head.

text_flags.why: near certain: the initial ca- is lost; 'catvāriṃśat-śatam' is the number 140 and the three parts then add to 360 as in 108
possible: the final m of śatam is printed at the head of the next word (spacing slip)

notes: 140 + 120 + 100 = 360, matching 108 (arithmetic given as evidence for the flags). Words restored: sa-viṃśa-śatam (sa = 'with', so 'a hundred with twenty') and antarādhau; the print has 'sa' separate and the m misplaced. antarādhi = trunk, the middle of the body (probable). Printed 'mūrddhnīti' = mūrdhni iti.
lines_deva: तेषां च त्वारिंशच्छतं शाखासु स विंशशत मंतराधौ शतं मूर्द्ध्नीति
lines_iast: teṣāṃ ca tvāriṃśacchataṃ śākhāsu sa viṃśaśata maṃtarādhau śataṃ mūrddhnīti

words.gloss: first part of ekaika-, 'each single' (print split)
second part of ekaikasmin, 'in each single' (print split)

hindi: वहाँ एक-एक सक्थि यानी निचले अंग में पाँच पादनख, प्रत्येक अंगुली में तीन अस्थियाँ, वे पन्द्रह।
english: There, in each single leg (sakthi): five foot-nails (pādanakha); in each toe three bones; those are fifteen.

text_flags.why: possible: the words are split wrongly in the print (ekaikasmin) and carry a stray final -a

notes: Reading: tatra ekaikasmin sakthini; the print splits ekaikasmin over two tokens, so the first half is given to the first token and the second half to 'kasmina'. 'sakthi' = thigh or whole leg; here the lower limb. 'tāni pañcadaśa' ('those are fifteen') is taken as the three bones of each of five toes (3 x 5); the Sanskrit does not say which items it counts. The nails are counted among the bones as printed. 'nakhāḥpratyekam' is run together in the print (split without a flag).
lines_deva: तत्रैकै कस्मिन सक्थिनि पंच पादनखाःप्रत्येकमंगुल्यां त्रीण्यस्थीनि तानि पंचदश
lines_iast: tatraikai kasmina sakthini paṃca pādanakhāḥpratyekamaṃgulyāṃ trīṇyasthīni tāni paṃcadaśa

words.gloss: kūrca (a part of the foot; sense uncertain); ankle; shank
heel (on a conjectural reading); knee; thigh

hindi: पाँच पादशलाकाएँ, उनका एक प्रतिबन्धक, कूर्च, गुल्फ और जंघा में दो-दो, तथा, अनुमानित पाठ पर, एड़ी, जानु और ऊरु में एक-एक।
english: Five foot-rods (pādaśalākā); one binder of them; two each in the kūrca, ankle (gulpha) and shank (jaṅghā); and, on a conjectural reading, one each in the heel, knee (jānu) and thigh (ūru).

text_flags.why: possible: pāṇi (hand) does not suit the leg, and the compound would not have visarga/r; pārṣṇi (heel) fits the list of leg places

notes: Continues the count of the leg begun in 110: 5 nails + 15 toe-bones + 5 rods + 1 binder + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 35, which is a quarter of the 140 in 109 (arithmetic as evidence only). 'śalākā' = rod, splint; 'kūrca' is kept untranslated (sense uncertain). The printed 'pāṇi' is the word for hand; the heel reading is hedged. Print: doubled cc in 'kūrcca' normalised. 'tat' in tatpratibandhaka is taken to refer to the rods.
lines_deva: पंचपादशलाकाः तत्प्रतिबंधकमेकं द्वे द्वे कूर्च्चगुल्फजंघास्वेकैकं पाणिर्जानूरुषु
lines_iast: paṃcapādaśalākāḥ tatpratibaṃdhakamekaṃ dve dve kūrccagulphajaṃghāsvekaikaṃ pāṇirjānūruṣu

hindi: और नख-अस्थि आदि सभी, सक्थि के समान, दोनों बाहुओं में भी।
english: And all, beginning with the nail-bones, as in the leg, also in the two arms.
notes: Elliptical: copula understood. Printed 'sarvāṇica' = sarvāṇi ca and 'sakthivadvāhvośca' = sakthi-vat bāhvoḥ ca (v/b interchange is common in the print, 'vāhvoḥ' for bāhvoḥ normalised). 'nakhāsthyādīni' is taken as 'beginning with nail(-bone)s', as in 110.

hindi: चौबीस पर्शुकाएँ यानी पसलियाँ।
english: Twenty-four parśukās (ribs).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. Counts as printed (24); the line does not say whether it is per side or in all.

hindi: उतने ही उनके स्थालक यानी छोटी थालियाँ और अर्बुद यानी उभार हैं।
english: Just as many are their sthālakas (small dishes) and arbudas (lumps).
notes: Copula understood. 'their' (tat-) refers to the ribs of 113. sthālaka and arbuda are not firmly identified in modern anatomy (probably the cup-like and knob-like articulating ends of the ribs, a guess, not stated). arbuda elsewhere means tumour; here 'lump' is kept literal.

hindi: तीस पीठ में।
english: Thirty in the back.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood.

words.gloss: in the bhaga (pubic or pudendal region, probable)

hindi: एक-एक भग यानी सम्भवतः जघन-क्षेत्र में और त्रिक यानी सम्भवतः कमर के पीछे के त्रिक-स्थान में।
english: One each in the bhaga (probably the pubic region) and the trika (probably the sacral region).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. bhaga usually means the female genitals; as a place for a bone it is read as the pubic region, which is probable but not certain. trika as in 106.

words.gloss: in the two hips or buttocks (nitamba; standard)

hindi: और दोनों नितम्बों में दो।
english: And two in the two nitambas (hips).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. Whether 'two' is the total or per side is not stated.

hindi: उसी प्रकार, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अक्षक यानी सम्भवतः हँसली, अंस यानी कन्धे और अंसफलक यानी कन्धे की चपटी हड्डियों में।
english: Likewise, on a conjectural reading, in the akṣaka (probably the collarbone), the shoulder (aṃsa) and the shoulder-blades (aṃsaphalaka).

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'kaṃsāṃsa' looks like a slip for kāṃsāṃsa (akṣaka + aṃsa + aṃsaphalaka); the book's own form could also be read akṣa-kaṃsa; sense not firm

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. 'Likewise' means 'in the same number as in 118'; the number is not repeated and is not supplied. The reading of the compound is uncertain (see text_flags); aṃsaphalaka = shoulder-blade (scapula, standard).

words.gloss: jatru (the region of the collarbone and root of the neck); palate (tālu)

hindi: वैसे ही गण्ड यानी गाल, कर्ण यानी कान और शंख यानी कनपटी में, तथा जत्रु यानी हँसली के स्थान और तालु में।
english: Likewise in the cheeks (gaṇḍa), ears and temples (śaṅkha), and in the jatru (collarbone region) and the palate (tālu).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. 'Likewise' repeats the number of 118/119, not restated. jatru = collarbone or the region where the neck meets the shoulder (probable). śaṅkha = temple (also 'conch').

hindi: तेरह गर्दन में, चार कण्ठनाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः श्वासनली में, दो हनुबन्धन में; बत्तीस दाँत और उसी प्रकार उलूखल यानी सम्भवतः दाँतों के गड्ढे; तीन नाक में, छह सिर में।
english: Thirteen in the neck; four in the kaṇṭhanāḍī (probably the windpipe), two in the jaw-joints (hanubandhana); thirty-two teeth, and likewise ulūkhalas (probably tooth-sockets); three in the nose, six in the head.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. 'tadvat' means 'as many' (thirty-two sockets for thirty-two teeth); the number is not repeated. ulūkhala = mortar; as the socket of a tooth it is probable. Print: 'kaṃṭhanāḍyāṃdve' joins two words (kaṇṭhanāḍyām dve; split without a flag). 'hanubandhane' is taken as the two jaw-joints (dual).
lines_deva: त्रयोदश ग्रीवायां चत्वारि कंठनाड्यांद्वे हनुबंधने द्वात्रिंशद्दंताः तद्वदुलूखलानि च त्रीणि नासायां षट् शिरसि
lines_iast: trayodaśa grīvāyāṃ catvāri kaṃṭhanāḍyāṃdve hanubaṃdhane dvātriṃśaddaṃtāḥ tadvadulūkhalāni ca trīṇi nāsāyāṃ ṣaṭ śirasi

words.gloss: knee; hip; shoulder; cheek; palate; temple; groin; middle; head

hindi: वे जानु, नितम्ब, अंस, गण्ड, तालु, शंख, वंक्षण, मध्य और सिरों में स्थित कपाल नाम वाले हैं।
english: Those in the knees, hips, shoulders, cheeks, palate, temples, groin, middle and heads are named kapāla (plates).
notes: 'tāni' refers to the bones counted in 115-121 at these places. The list is a locative dvandva; 'madhya' (middle) is kept as printed with no further sense, and the divisions 'vaṅkṣaṇamadhya' (middle of the groin) are possible. kapāla = potsherd, plate, also skull; here the name of one class of bone (see 127). Copula understood.

hindi: दाँत तो रुचक हैं।
english: The teeth (daśana), however, are rucakas (a class of bone).
notes: Copula understood. rucaka is one of the classes of bone (see 127) and is kept untranslated.

words.gloss: nose; ear; neck; eye; sheath, socket
taruṇas (tender ones; the taruṇa bones are usually taken as cartilage, probable)

hindi: घ्राण, कर्ण, ग्रीवा और अक्षिकोश में तरुण यानी कोमल अस्थियाँ हैं, जो सम्भवतः उपास्थि हैं।
english: In the nose, ears, neck and eye-sockets (akṣikoṣa) are the taruṇas (tender ones, usually taken as cartilage, probable).
notes: Copula understood. The printed 'grīvā'kṣi' has an avagraha after -ā (print habit, no flag). 'taruṇa' = young, tender; the modern identification as cartilage is probable. akṣikoṣa = eye-sheath, taken as eye-socket (probable).

hindi: पाणि, पाद, पार्श्व और पृष्ठ में वलय यानी छल्ले जैसी हड्डियाँ हैं।
english: In the hands, feet, sides and back are the valayas (rings).
notes: Copula understood. 'valaya' = ring; the class of bone is named after its shape, and no further explanation is added. (The Hindi 'छल्ले जैसी हड्डियाँ' only restates the name valaya, rings.)

hindi: शेष नलक यानी नली जैसी हैं।
english: The remaining ones are nalakas (tubes).
notes: Copula understood. The closing 'iti' marks the end of the classification and is not translated. nalaka = a small tube or reed; the class of tubular bones is the usual reading (probable).

hindi: क्योंकि उनमें सिराओं और स्नायुओं से मांस बँधे हुए हैं।
english: For in them the fleshes (masses of flesh) are bound by vessels (sirā) and snāyus (ligaments).
notes: 'teṣu' refers to the bones. The plural māṃsāni is kept as 'fleshes' (flesh-masses, perhaps muscles); no word is added. sirā = vein or vessel; snāyu = ligament, sinew (both standard).
lines_deva: तेषु हि सिराभिः स्नायुभिश्च निबद्धानि मांसानि
lines_iast: teṣu hi sirābhiḥ snāyubhiśca nibaddhāni māṃsāni

hindi: अस्थि-सन्धियों की संख्या दो सौ दस।
english: Two hundred, in excess by ten (that is, two hundred and ten), of the joints of bones (asthi-sandhi).
notes: Count as printed: 200 plus 10 = 210. Elliptical: no verb; the line states a number of joints and 'number' is not in the Sanskrit (the Hindi 'संख्या' is the natural gloss of the genitive and adds only that). Copula understood.
